summary: Iteration 8 backend tests for auto-start attendance + selfie challenge lifecycle. New test file /app/backend/tests/test_auto_start.py with 15 tests covering: auto-start success + challenge count, disabled setting, outside-geofence 403, low-accuracy 400, session-already-active 400, approved time-off block, challenge triggering via ping, respond success (+ photo persistence via /api/photos/session/<sid>::<cid>), unknown challenge 404, respond-after-deadline flagging, expiry via ping + selfie_missed security_event high, fixed-mode planning, and regression for manual /sessions/start (photo + challenges). All 15 pass in isolation.

minor.issue: Class silently absorbs 5 stray fields (selfie_challenges_per_shift, selfie_response_window_minutes, selfie_mode, selfie_fixed_times, auto_start_on_entry) because lines 175-179 are orphan-indented right after a bare comment. Python interprets them as continuation of the previous class body. Verified via `TimeOffDecision.model_fields`. No behavioural bug today (all Optional + ignored) but the model contract is wrong.

Trailing block (lines 206-210) mistakenly appends resume_window_hours/accuracy_tolerance_meters/max_speed_kmh/spoof_sensitivity/notify_admin_on_spoof to ChallengeResponse. These fields belong to OrgSettingsUpdate and should be removed. Confirmed via `ChallengeResponse.model_fields`.

action_items: Clean up /app/backend/models.py: delete the orphan block on lines 174-179 (duplicate of OrgSettingsUpdate fields) and trim the trailing lines 206-210 on ChallengeResponse. The correct ChallengeResponse should only expose `face_photo`.
critical_code_review_comments: models.py has been damaged by a bad edit: orphan-indented fields after `TimeOffDecision` silently merge into its schema (Python treats them as class continuation because the intervening line is only a comment). Also ChallengeResponse has 5 unrelated fields appended after face_photo. Neither breaks the runtime today (fields are Optional and unused), but they widen the public API contract in an unsafe way and will confuse OpenAPI consumers.

sessions.py `/challenge/{id}/respond`: if challenges array is populated but the specific challenge isn't the one being pinged, mutating a copy still works because dicts are references — fine. However, the deadline branch uses `<` (respond_by_ms < now_ms) whereas the ping-sweep uses `<`. Consider `<=` for exact-second boundary consistency.
sessions.py `/auto-start` does NOT call log_security_event for geofence/accuracy denies (whereas /start does). Audit parity should be preserved.

sessions.py `_plan_challenges` fixed-mode branch computes today's HH:MM in UTC only — fine for a 60min shift near midnight it can still slip below start_ms and silently drop; the fall-back to random then fires, which matches the spec but is subtle. Documented behaviour is fine.

Full test suite in parallel (`pytest tests/`) has 4 failures caused by cross-file xdist shared-employee-session contamination (time-off + active-session state bleed between files). Pre-existing; each file passes in isolation. Consider per-file fixture cleanup or scoping employee login per-file with a `sessions/reset` in an autouse fixture.

Two cosmetic-but-real models.py bugs (extra fields on TimeOffDecision + ChallengeResponse) reported for main agent to strip. When running the entire /app/backend/tests folder in one shot, expect 4 cross-file failures due to xdist parallelism on a single shared employee account (test_photos.live_endpoint / accuracy tests + one auto_start test); running per-file passes all.
rca of the issue: models.py file appears to have been generated by concatenating a diff on top of an incomplete section: the `# ---------- Org Settings ----------` header on line 174 was written before its class definition, so the intended OrgSettingsUpdate fields on lines 175-179 landed at module-level indentation. Because Python only closes a class body at the next non-indented statement (comments do not count), those five fields silently attach to the preceding `TimeOffDecision` class. Similarly the tail block (lines 206-210) is leftover from a paste of OrgSettingsUpdate and attached itself to ChallengeResponse. Fix: delete lines 174-179 entirely and truncate ChallengeResponse to just `face_photo`.
